claim: *Observation and intent answer different questions.* The observed system can reveal that A calls C; the decision model can state whether that relationship is permitted. Agreement establishes correspondence, not correctness.

topology.description: Two peer graphs distinguish observed calls from declared permissions; missing policyedge labeled, not drawn as permitted.

required_terms: Observed system Does A call C?
Declared policy May A call C?
bw_encoding: Black outlines and arrows; white nodes; sparse 3–7% gray groups. Every non-solid relation is locally labeled; no distinction depends on color.
redesign: Native semantic redraw; colors replaced by labeled relations and line conventions.
alt: Two panels compare observed calls with declared permissions. The implementation has A-to-B and A-to-C calls. The model declares A-to-B but marks A-to-C as absent with a cross. Agreement establishes correspondence, not correctness. The candidate uses black lines, white backgrounds and sparse gray; meaning does not depend on color.
